rows.medi_said: لا- لازم ... عملتها or, uh, تعلّمتها
rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: Past obligation needs kaan + laazem; he said bare لازم and Amal recast the whole line with كان لازم and explained 'I had to'.
rows.english: I had to teach her everything

rows.why: He used تعلّم (learn, t-form, past) where 'teach her' needs علّم as a bare present after laazem; Amal recast أعلمها.

rows.chat: bas ana ra7 ajrreb a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a
rows.why: He used the command form خليها for 'I (will try to) let her'; Amal recast with the I-form أخليها.
rows.english: (I will try to) let her become

rows.medi_said: make her a good [speaking Arabic] Would it be [speaking Arabic] ?
rows.why: He could not produce 'employee' (sheet: employee | Muwazzaf | موظف) and Amal supplied موظفة; his own Arabic here is hidden by the engine.

rows.medi_said: اليوم الأربعاء. No. Yeah. يوم الأربعاء.
rows.why: He dropped his right اليوم الأربعاء for يوم الأربعاء; Amal said nothing, her chat keeps el-yoam el-arbi3a (reading mine).

rows.medi_said: to behamasu ki-- ... past tense. شو
rows.amal_said: No، it's present، بس it's one، not group of things. ... شو بيحمسك؟
rows.why: For 'what excites you' he used the plural verb behamasu; Amal said it is one thing, not a group, and gave شو بيحمسك which he repeated.

rows.amal_said: Made. ... Past. He made me excited.
rows.why: 'He made me excited' is past; he used present بيحمسني, Amal prompted 'Made... Past' and he said حمّسني.

rows.amal_said: Get excited, not excite me or someone. ... It's the wrong verb. It's get excited, not excite.
rows.why: For 'get excited' he used the make-X verb حمّس instead of the get-X تحمّس; Amal said it is the wrong verb.

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Okay. Uh, tetamasi.
rows.why: The command form takes one t- (t7ammasi); he added a second t- and Amal said 'No T, just one T'.

rows.amal_said: we are using the adjective here because it's are. Are you. You are excited. Aren't you excited? Meaning now.
rows.why: 'Why aren't you excited (now)' needs mish + the adjective mit7ammse, not ma + the habitual verb; Amal explained the rule.
'We got excited' needs the get-X verb تحمّسنا; he said حمّسنا (we excited someone), Amal only said Mm-hmm and her chat writes t7ammasna (reading mine).

rows.medi_said: في الشارع ... Or ala el shara? No, fi el shara.
rows.amal_said: street. What's the road? ... Like the way on the road.
rows.why: He used شارع (street) for 'on the road/on the way'; Amal said 'street. What's the road?' and he said على الطريق (sheet: road / way / route | 6ariq | طريق).

rows.amal_said: الـ safar. Safra is one trip. Safar is...
rows.why: For 'traveling' he used سفرة (one trip) instead of the noun سفر; Amal explained the difference and he said السفر.
'Excite me more' needs the object ending -ni; Amal prompted 'Me. Excite me.' and he said حمسيني اكتر.
With أنا, kaan must be كنت; Amal said كنت (engine قُنت) and he repeated أنا كنت أشتغل.
Showing you (a woman) takes the object ending -ki; he tried -k / -nek and Amal recast أفرجيكي, which he repeated.

rows.amal_said: is did I hurt you? Did you get hurt?
rows.why: 'Did you get hurt' takes no object; his -k ending made it 'did I hurt you', Amal said so and he moved to توجّعتي.

rows.amal_said: No, by me. ... Because of me.
rows.why: 'Hurt by me' on the get-verb needs مني, not the object ending -ni; Amal said 'No, by me' and he reached توجعتي مني, which she approved.
rows.english: Did you get hurt by me?

rows.why: 'Don't hurt her' needs the make-X verb وجّع; he used the get-X تتوجع with -ha, Amal repeated the prompt, said 'very close', and he landed on ما توجعيها.
Negative command is ma + the you-form (t-) with the object -ha; he said ما وجعي, Amal said 'very close' and he fixed it to ما توجعيها.

rows.medi_said: bidayai, بدايي ... شو بدايايي or بدايي؟
rows.amal_said: So what upsets you? So the what is the he, and then upsets you.
rows.why: In 'what upsets you' the subject 'what' is he, so the verb is beydaay2ek; he used the I-form بضايق, Amal named the rule and he said شو بدايقك.

rows.medi_said: همّة؟ daya u-- daya u ni. Daya u ni.
rows.why: 'Did they upset you' needs -ki, not -ni (me); Amal prompted 'You' and he said daya u ki.
'What did you get upset about' needs the get-X تضايقتي (her chat etdaaya2ti); he said ضايقتي (you upset someone) and Amal let it pass - may be the engine dropping the t.
rows.english: What did you get upset about?

rows.why: Amal's chat writes illi 3meltih with the pointer -h back to 'what'; he said اللي عملتي without it. Her voiced عملت is unclear, so filed as let-pass (reading mine).

rows.amal_said: بي. ... كان بيضايق not ت 'cause it makes people upset. It upsets.
rows.why: 'Was upsetting' (made people upset) needs the make-X verb يضايق after kaan, not the get-X اتضايق/يتضايق; Amal named it ('not ت ... it upsets').

rows.medi_said: ما تتدايقي ـيها، ما i ha.
rows.why: 'Don't upset her' needs the make-X verb (her chat ma tdaay2iha); he ended on the get-X تتضايقي + -ha and Amal said ممتاز (reading mine).
The sentence was about 'they'; he said هو and Amal prompted 'They', he said همّ.
rows.english: I think they got upset with us

rows.chat: immi tdaaya2at minni 3ashaan ma shufetha el-usboo3 el-maadi
rows.why: 'I didn't see her' is ma shufetha; he said mashufeta, Amal recast شفتها and he asked 'what?' then repeated - may only be a dropped h (S4).
Noun + adjective phrase needs el- on both (el-usboo3 el-maadi, in her chat and her voiced line at 54:44 just before); he dropped it on the noun and she did not react.

rows.amal_said: These are the last two ones.
rows.why: 'The last verb' is aa5er + noun with no el- (A15); he said الآخر ... فعل and Amal answered in English without fixing it (reading mine).
rows.english: Is this the last T verb?

rows.medi_said: البالـ... الـ، الـ بالعكس ... ما عنده بالعكس
rows.amal_said: ما عنده عكس. آه. ... بس hacks on its own is like the noun for opposite.
rows.why: He used the expression بالعكس (on the contrary) where the noun عكس (opposite) was needed; Amal recast ما عنده عكس and explained (sheet: opposite (bel-3aks = on the contrary) | 3aks | عكس).
Speaking to Amal (a woman) he used the feminine verb but the masculine ending halak; her chat writes 7arrki 7aalek; her voiced حرك حالك was not a fix of that (reading mine).
Moving something to the right takes la-, not 3ala; Amal recast 'La el yameen' and explained 3ala is for giving directions.
rows.english: I moved my bed to the right

rows.amal_said: Ashya ak or ashya ek. Ashya e.
rows.why: 'Your things' is plural ashyaa2ek; he put the ending on singular ishi (sheet: thing | Eshi | اشي) and Amal gave the plural.

rows.medi_said: وين راح وين راح بتحر... بتحركي
rows.why: After ra7 the verb is bare (ra7 t7arrki); he kept the b- and Amal recast تحركي (engine wrote نوبي before it).

rows.medi_said: وين راح وين راح بتحر... بتحركي
rows.amal_said: هذي الطاولة. And it's لوين. ... It's لوين. We added to the question to always.
rows.why: 'Where ... to' puts la- in front of the question word (lawain); he said وين and Amal named the rule.
rows.english: Where (to) will you move this table?

rows.medi_said: هذا الطويل، To is على؟ ... What's that?
rows.why: For 'table' he said الطويل (long) and asked 'what's that?'; Amal gave الطاولة (sheet: table | Tâwla | طاولة) - could be the engine for a near-sound.
طاولة is feminine so 'this' is هذي; Amal recast هذي الطاولة.

rows.amal_said: ورقة is feminine and one. ورق is plural.
rows.why: 'The papers' is the plural ورق; he used singular ورقة, Amal said ورقة is one and he switched to تحركوا.
rows.english: The papers moved from the wind

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] ... What'd I say? (Amal echo: عندهم)
rows.why: He asked 'What did I say?' and Amal echoed عندهم - he said 'they have' for 'we have' (engine hid his line); he then said لما عنّا.

rows.medi_said: nifarijini or نفرجـ... It's بفرجي؟ نفرجي؟
rows.why: Showing them the rugs needs the object -hom; he cycled nifarijini / بفرجي / نفرجي and Amal supplied فرجيهم.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] [laughs] Does that, does that not work?
rows.amal_said: الله يعافيكي بس. ... أو الله يعافيكي ألف مرة
rows.why: He answered her يعطيك ألف عافية with a phrase hidden by the engine and asked 'does that not work?'; Amal gave the set reply الله يعافيكي.
rows.english: (reply to) thank you for your effort
